Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

tell off verb

scold

also scold, chew out, give someone a telling-off, reprimand, why did he chew you out?

classical

Cic. Cael. 25: objurgāvit M. Caelium, sīcut nēminem umquam parēns (Lewis & Short)

objurgō, objurgāre, objurgāvī, objurgātum

verb, first conjugation

scold, tell off, reprove

Lewis & Short: to chide, scold, rebuke (frequent and classical).

Other words

  • pilō, pilāre — given for “chew out”

    verb, first conjugation · avoid · post-classical · Petr. 43.4: malam parram pilāvit (Lewis & Short, a doubtful reading); Traupman 95

    Traupman gives it for “why did the instructor chew you out?”. Lewis & Short knows pilāre only as to strip of hair and, rarely and late, to plunder; it is not a word for scolding.

Examples

  • monendī amīcī saepe sunt et objurgandī

    friends must often be advised, and told offCic. Lael. 88 (Lewis & Short)

SourcesLewis & Short: objurgo · Lewis & Short: pilo
